label: Horror subgenres
blurb: You can like several of these and dislike the rest, which is exactly why they are a tree and not a ladder.

nodes.label: Slasher
nodes.blurb: A killer, a group and a body count. The most formalised structure in the genre, and the easiest to see broken on purpose.

nodes.label: Giallo
nodes.blurb: Italian, gloved, and lit in colours no room has ever been. Style as the point rather than as decoration.

nodes.label: Folk Horror
nodes.blurb: Landscape, old custom and a community that is not going to help you. Daylight is not a comfort here.

nodes.label: Cosmic Horror
nodes.blurb: The threat is scale, not intent. Adapts badly and often, which is half of what makes it interesting to follow.

nodes.label: Body Horror
nodes.blurb: Transformation, prosthetics and practical effects doing work no render has matched. The subgenre most tied to a craft.

nodes.label: Found Footage
nodes.blurb: A camera inside the story. Cheap enough that anyone can attempt it, which is why the range in quality is enormous.

nodes.label: Creature Feature
nodes.blurb: Something large and hostile, built in a workshop. The direct ancestor of every suit and every animatronic.

nodes.label: J-Horror
nodes.blurb: Quiet, domestic, and about the wrong thing being in the room with you. Reshaped the whole genre after 1998.

edges.note: The slasher's rules were largely imported from giallo, one film at a time.
